clue.text: Risky behaviour allowed in activity of serious nature, mostly

indicators.note: in places the word for allowed inside the rearranged letters
activity suggests the letters are busily stirred up and set in a new order
mostly means the word nature loses its final letter

parts.note: allowed means let, as in permitted

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dangerous gamble while engaged in some grave undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'activity of' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal; 'mostly' trims the final E from nature before the scramble, and the permitted word sits between the third and fourth letters from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The game of spinning a revolver's chamber and firing at oneself is the byword for reckless gambling.

clue.text: Pragmatic attitude is evident in kingdom

indicators.note: evident in says the word is shows up inside the word for kingdom

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom

explanation.surface: A practical outlook is apparent throughout some monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A down-to-earth, practical view of things, accepting how matters actually are, is a synonym.

clue.text: Bridge team in trail to get financial supporter

indicators.note: in places the bridge pair inside the word for trail

parts.note: a spoor is an animal's track or trail
in bridge, North and South form one partnership, abbreviated NS

explanation.surface: A bridge pair following a trail ends up finding a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer who pays money towards an event or person in return for publicity is a synonym.

clue.text: About to complete tour without appeal

definitions.meaning: someone nearing the end of a holiday tour is staying at its final holiday resort
a court of last resort is one whose decision cannot be appealed further

explanation.surface: A traveller near the end of a trip finds it has lost its charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without appeal' looks like 'unattractive', but it is the legal sense: nothing further to appeal to.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a final recourse, after which no further appeal or option remains.

clue.text: Locations investing in web in this part of the world

indicators.note: investing in means going into, so the locations are placed inside the word for web

parts.note: a net is a web of mesh
areas are locations or districts

explanation.surface: Places are putting money into the internet in some region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing in' looks financial but means 'going inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: The region around the eastern Mediterranean, from Turkey to Egypt, is so called.

clue.text: 'Ring' composer I ignored — 'Ring' is to be excessive

parts.note: a ring is the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: ignored means the letter I is dropped from the composer's name

parts.note: Verdi was the Italian opera composer
again a ring is the letter O

explanation.surface: Taking out an 'I' from the Ring composer's name seems to be overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Ring' composer suggests Wagner, but the composer is Verdi; each 'Ring' is a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something too far, using too much of it, is a synonym for going to excess.

clue.text: Redevelopment of a callow, inferior part of Mexico

indicators.note: redevelopment rebuilds the given words, so their letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Rebuilding a raw, second-rate district somewhere in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baja California peninsula of north-west Mexico is also known by this English name.

clue.text: Zero expression of disgust in game or puzzle

indicators.note: in places the zero and the exclamation inside the word for game

parts.note: a tie is a match or game, as in a cup tie
zero is the figure O
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone shows zero enthusiasm, grunting in disgust at a game or brainteaser.
explanation.walkthrough: A tie is a match in a knockout cup competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding brainteaser, and the very name of the Telegraph's harder crossword series, which this is.

clue.text: Dogs' and pigs' tails — and what they do?

definitions.text: Dogs' and pigs' tails — and what they do?

parts.words: Dogs' and pigs' tails — and what they do?
parts.note: tails are the final parts of words; the words dogs and pigs each finish with the letters G and S

explanation.surface: A question about animals' tails and what those tails get up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Tails here are word endings: 'dogs' and 'pigs' both END IN GS, which run together spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tails or final parts of words, stories or things are their conclusions or closes.

clue.text: Change of opinion fine in a fight expert

indicators.note: in places the fine abbreviation inside the run of a, fight and expert

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or fight
an ace is an expert
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fighting expert does a sudden U-turn after being fined.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete reversal of one's position or view, from the military command to turn around.

clue.text: Welsh corgi, say, not initially hurt

indicators.note: not initially means the dog word loses its first letter

parts.note: a corgi is an example of a dog, or hound

explanation.surface: A Welsh corgi apparently wasn't hurt at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh corgi' reads as one breed, but the words split: Welsh gives W and corgi is a hound.
explanation.definitionFit: Injured, as in the past tense of the verb to injure with a blade or bullet.

clue.text: Magazine is certain to cancel run

indicators.note: to cancel means the run abbreviation is struck out of the word for certain

parts.note: sure means certain
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A magazine is sure to scrap its print run.
explanation.definitionFit: A single number of a periodical, such as the March edition of a monthly, is called this.

clue.text: Ponder varying hydrogen in body chemical

indicators.note: varying means the letters change their arrangement

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemist muses on hydrogen changing within some bodily compound.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hormones released by the brain that relieve pain and lift mood, as after exercise.

clue.text: Fellow's enveloped in gloom in Russian city

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside the word for gloom

parts.note: murk is darkness or gloom
a fellow is a man, so fellow's gives man's

explanation.surface: A man wrapped in darkness in a city of northern Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: This port on the Kola Peninsula, beyond the Arctic Circle, is a city of Russia.

clue.text: French are occupying vehicles, showing neck

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside the word for vehicles

parts.note: cars are vehicles
es is the French for 'are', as in tu es, you are

explanation.surface: French people are filling cars, displaying their necks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' is the verb: to kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To neck is to kiss and fondle amorously, so a tender stroke or embrace is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Airline no longer involved in major effort in warm weather

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside the word for major effort

parts.note: a heave is a mighty effort or push
TWA, Trans World Airlines, was an American airline that no longer exists

explanation.surface: A defunct airline was caught up in some huge push during a hot spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of unusually hot weather lasting days or weeks is called this.

clue.text: Record captured by tax assistant

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the word for tax

parts.note: a duty is a tax, as on imports
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A recording seized by the tax authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command who stands in for a superior is a type of helper.

clue.text: Father consumed by endless passion and gloom

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the shortened passion word
endless means the word for passion loses its last letter

parts.note: desire is passion
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A father eaten up by unending passion and misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopelessness, utter loss of hope, is a deep form of gloominess.

clue.text: As poultry, initially, producing eggs

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of poultry is used

parts.note: hens laying are producing eggs

explanation.surface: Speaking of poultry, they are first of all laying eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is the definition, in the theatrical sense: 'Olivier as Hamlet' means Olivier acting that role.
explanation.definitionFit: In cast lists 'as' means taking the role of, acting the part of a character.

clue.text: Accepts fiction volume penned by busy people

indicators.note: penned by means shut inside the word for busy people

parts.note: bees are proverbially busy, so busy people are bees
a lie is a fiction or untruth

explanation.surface: A work of fiction written by hard-working authors gets accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' suggests writing, but means enclosed, as in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something as true, to give credence to it, is to accept it.

clue.text: Volume in anger rising, revealing bitter stuff

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word for anger is read upwards

parts.note: rage is anger

explanation.surface: Noise growing louder as anger mounts shows sourness.
explanation.definitionFit: This sour condiment made from fermented wine or cider is literally sharp-tasting stuff.

clue.text: Cloud begins to rise, surrounding third of mountains

indicators.note: surrounding means the turned word goes round the single letter
to rise in a down clue means the word for begins is read upwards

parts.note: starts means begins

indicators.note: third of means the third letter of mountains is taken

explanation.surface: A cloud starts to climb, wrapping round part of a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A low flat grey layer of cloud covering the sky is this type, a meteorological term.

clue.text: Queen enthralled by party crowd in county

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive inside the words for party and crowd

parts.note: a do is a party
a set is a crowd or group of people
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A queen is captivated by a party crowd somewhere in the shires.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county on England's south coast, one of its administrative shires.

clue.text: Person made responsible, positioned to receive top personality

indicators.note: to receive means the word for positioned takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: sat means placed or positioned
a cap is a top or lid
ego is one's self or personality

explanation.surface: Someone is set up to welcome a celebrity and ends up taking the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blamed for the wrongs of others, from the biblical goat sent into the wilderness bearing sins.

clue.text: One has a bad time when daughter leaves

indicators.note: when daughter leaves means the daughter abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: a downer is a depressing experience or bad time

explanation.surface: A parent has a miserable spell when their daughter moves out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has' looks like the start of a sentence, but is the definition: one who has something.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is one who has or holds something as property.

clue.text: Is the writer ready for a Spanish associate?

parts.note: the writer is I, the setter; is the writer becomes the question am I
go means ready and working, as in all systems go

explanation.surface: An author asks whether they are prepared for a Spanish friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish for friend is commonly used in English for a pal or companion.

clue.text: This time with gang, drunk? Last chance of freedom!

indicators.note: drunk means the letters reel about into a new order

explanation.surface: Out with the lads and drinking hard: one final fling before marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom's party with male friends on the eve of a wedding is jokingly his final taste of liberty.

clue.text: Dicky sought treasures in reference book

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A man named Dicky hunted for treasure in a reference work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name, but is the slang adjective for unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Mark Roget compiled the famous English book of synonyms grouped by idea.
